title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
summary: SpaceX successfully launched its Starship for the 13th suborbital test flight on July 24, addressing issues from the previous attempt and deploying functioning satellites for the first time.

title: ULA deals with financial challenges caused by Vulcan grounding
summary: United Launch Alliance secured a loan from its corporate parents to address financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. The company is navigating these difficulties as it awaits the rocket's return to flight.

title: LatConnect 60 Unveils Proprietary AI Capabilities Following Growing Indo-Pacific Defence Interest in SWIRSAT
summary: LatConnect 60 introduced proprietary AI-driven intelligence-fusion capabilities amid rising defense interest in its SWIRSAT program within the Indo-Pacific region. The Australian satellite Earth observation and AI company aims to enhance its offerings following increased demand.

title: Office of Space Commerce to move ahead on mission authorization
summary: The Commerce Department is advancing a voluntary mission authorization system for novel space activities not regulated by other agencies. This initiative aims to fill regulatory gaps in emerging space missions.

title: Lightning strikes Long March 3B after liftoff, Kinetica-1 launches 5 satellites
summary: A Long March 3B rocket successfully delivered its payload to orbit despite being struck by lightning shortly after liftoff. Separately, the Kinetica-1 rocket launched five satellites.
company: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)

title: EU delays release of Copernicus imagery over Gulf of Oman
summary: The European Union delayed the release of certain Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery for 24 hours at the request of the U.S. due to concerns over the Gulf of Oman. This decision highlights potential geopolitical sensitivities in satellite data dissemination.

title: Air Force takes over troubled military GPS receiver program
summary: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center will now oversee the development, integration, and sustainment of military GPS receiver equipment. This move aims to address issues with the program accessing the military's encrypted GPS signal.
company: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center

title: NASA programs feel effects of workforce reductions
summary: NASA reports that over two dozen major projects have been impacted by a 20% reduction in its civil servant workforce over the past year. The workforce reductions are causing delays and disruptions across multiple programs.

title: Poland commits $745 million to EU’s IRIS² constellation project
summary: Poland has committed $745 million to the EU's IRIS² satellite internet constellation project. The investment aims to support the development of a multi-orbit satellite internet system.

title: Mark Matossian co-founds Whipsmart Ventures to fund space and deep tech
summary: Mark Matossian has co-founded Whipsmart Ventures, a venture capital fund aimed at investing in space and deep tech startups. The fund is supported by a software engineer and a best-selling author.

title: An off-the-shelf camera could help us find more black holes smashing together
summary: A new off-the-shelf camera could enhance the detection of black hole collisions by improving LIGO's instrumentation without requiring new technology development. This innovation addresses an existing problem in gravitational wave detection.

title: NASA astronaut, 2 cosmonauts returning to Earth on July 26: Watch it live
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Russian cosmonauts will return to Earth from the International Space Station on July 26. Their homecoming can be watched live.

title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket makes the 'softest splashdown' ever after launching next-gen Starlink satellites in Flight 13 test (video)
summary: SpaceX's Starship megarocket successfully completed its 13th test flight, achieving the 'softest splashdown' ever after launching next-gen Starlink satellites. The mission marked a significant milestone with a surprising successful conclusion.

title: ZWO Seestar S30 Pro smart telescope review
summary: The ZWO Seestar S30 Pro is a compact, automated smart telescope featuring a higher resolution upgrade. This review highlights its advanced capabilities and design improvements.

title: We boldly chat with 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' showrunners about space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors for season 4 (interview)
summary: The showrunners of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discuss incorporating space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors into season 4. They express enthusiasm for the creative challenge of including dinosaurs in the series.

title: What lurks beneath the volcanoes of Jupiter's moon Io? NASA's Juno probe just took a peek
summary: NASA's Juno probe has provided new insights into the subsurface of Jupiter's moon Io, revealing details about its volcanoes that could reshape volcanic studies across the solar system, including Earth. These findings may transform how scientists understand volcanic activity beyond our planet.

title: Planet hunter gets the silent treatment | Space photo of the day for July 24, 2026
summary: ESA's Plato spacecraft has completed critical testing ahead of its upcoming spaceflight. The mission aims to hunt for exoplanets and study their host stars.

title: Lightning strike on Chinese rocket captured in epic launch photo
summary: A Chinese Long March-3B rocket was struck by lightning shortly after liftoff, yet the launch successfully deployed its satellite payload into orbit.

title: This Week In Space LIVE: The Viking Mars landings 50 years later
summary: A live event titled 'This Week In Space' will air on July 24 at 1:30 p.m. ET to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Viking Mars landings.

title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Snaps Family Portrait of Earth, Moon
summary: NASA's ESCAPADE spacecraft captured images of Earth and the Moon during its journey to Mars. The photos were taken from a distance of 363,250 miles from Earth and 115,600 miles from the Moon.

title: New Crew Members Welcomed to International Space Station
summary: Three new crew members—Anna Kikina and Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos, and Anil Menon of NASA—arrived at the International Space Station on July 14, 2026. They were welcomed aboard the ISS on July 18, 2026, after launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome.

title: NASA Announces New Spacecraft Technology Demonstration Mission at Moon
summary: NASA announced a new spacecraft technology demonstration mission at the Moon, partnering with industry to advance cislunar infrastructure for the Artemis program. The CAPSTONE 02 mission, awarded to Advanced Space, will test rendezvous, autonomous navigation, and communication capabilities.

title: NASA to Support Blue Origin New Glenn Rocket Testing, Advance Artemis
summary: NASA and Blue Origin agreed to conduct second stage hot fire testing for Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket at NASA's Stennis Space Center. This collaboration supports NASA's Artemis program through a reimbursable Space Act Agreement.

title: Hubble Spies One-Sided Spiral
summary: Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of spiral galaxy NGC 4654, located 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. The galaxy's asymmetric structure may be influenced by interactions with intergalactic gas.

title: A Million-Panel Project
summary: Utah has inaugurated a massive solar power and battery storage facility, featuring a million panels. The project is one of the largest in the region.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4954–4960: Celebrating Our Rover Engineers Past and Present
summary: The Curiosity rover team celebrates the contributions of past and present engineers. The blog highlights the APXS instrument's role in measuring rock chemistry during mission operations.

title: Look for NASA+ Now Streaming on Amazon Fire TV
summary: NASA+ is now available on Amazon Fire TV Channels, expanding access to its streaming content. Customers can use Alexa+ to view NASA programming on compatible devices.

title: Crews Move Artemis IV Liquid Hydrogen Tank
summary: NASA crews transported the 130-foot-tall Artemis IV liquid hydrogen tank from the Michoud Assembly Facility to a test building on May 15, 2026. The tank will be part of the core stage for the Artemis IV mission.

title: NASA’s MAVEN Illuminates New Understanding of Auroras at Mars
summary: NASA's MAVEN mission has revealed that auroras on Mars form similarly to those on Earth, providing new insights into the planet's atmospheric interactions. The findings, published in Nature Communications, highlight the shared mechanisms driving charged particle circulation in both planetary atmospheres.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, successfully launched on its third attempt, achieving new milestones for SpaceX. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship system.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew by three members. Additionally, a U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing challenges in the Starship program's development.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch Northrop Grumman's MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft from Florida. The Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV-1) aims to demonstrate in-space servicing capabilities.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new attempt at launching Starship Flight 13 after a previous aborted launch. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are scheduled for upcoming launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space are making progress on their respective launch vehicles: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5. While Starship's test program has been the recent focus, these companies continue advancing their rocket developments.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a milestone with the first successful recovery of a booster, and LandSpace is now aiming for its first land recovery.

title: Soyuz MS-29 launches new crew to ISS from Baikonur
summary: Soyuz MS-29 successfully launched a new crew to the International Space Station (ISS) from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. The mission marks another crewed flight to the orbiting laboratory.

title: Launch Preview: Soyuz to launch crew to ISS, Starship to fly another test flight
summary: Soyuz is set to launch a crew to the International Space Station (ISS), while SpaceX's Starship is preparing for its 13th flight test. Seven launches are scheduled globally this week.

summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary with a booklet highlighting 50 key achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's milestones in space exploration and technology.

summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance communication and radar systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber at ESTEC, confirming its electronics are fit for space. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket, scheduled for March 2027.

summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to discuss the implementation of CM25, the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025, aiming to inform industry about planned activities and priorities. These events will provide a platform for direct exchange between ESA and the industrial community.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: The article discusses a new robotic arm designed for space applications, highlighting its potential versatility and impact on future missions. This technology could revolutionize satellite servicing and in-space assembly.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and ASPIICS instrument are fully operational, resuming formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: ESA’s Prodex programme brings scientific research to space
summary: ESA's Prodex programme has enabled the successful launch of the 4DSpace-Daedalus mission in Norway. The programme supports research institutes in participating in European space science activities and missions.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step for Europe's involvement in lunar exploration.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, highlighting the intersection of the semiconductor industry and lunar exploration efforts. This move underscores the growing importance of advanced computing technology in space missions.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb program. The company's Next program may not yet be fully developed, according to FCC filings.

title: NASA Puts $2B Price Tag on Nuclear Mars Mission
summary: NASA has estimated a $2 billion cost for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft designed for interplanetary missions to Mars. This marks the first such initiative to use nuclear propulsion for deep space exploration.

title: Intel Authorization Act Proposes Limiting Commercial EO Access
summary: The Intel Authorization Act aims to restrict commercial Earth observation (EO) satellite operators from sharing certain data with the public. The US government asserts that EO data is a privilege, not a right, and seeks greater control over its dissemination.

title: The UK Scraps the Department in Charge of UKSA
summary: The UK has decided to abolish the department overseeing the UK Space Agency (UKSA) during the Farnborough Air Show. This move was announced by the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

title: The UK and Space Florida Launch Joint Fund
summary: The UK and Space Florida have launched a joint fund to support projects with partners from both regions. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between entities in the UK and Florida.

title: Breaking Down the $686B Space Economy
summary: The global space economy reached a record $686 billion in 2025, as reported by the Space Foundation. This marks significant growth in the industry.

title: FCC Eyes Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Bands for Satellites
summary: The FCC is considering a proposal to permit unlicensed wireless devices like Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to communicate directly with satellites. This move aims to expand satellite connectivity options for consumer devices.

title: deltaVision Raises €10.2M to Build In-Orbit Refueling Tech
summary: deltaVision has raised €10.2 million to develop in-orbit refueling technology. The funds will be used to expand manufacturing capacity and research new capabilities.

title: NASA to Support New Glenn Hot Fire Testing at Stennis Space Center
summary: NASA and Blue Origin will conduct second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at NASA’s Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. This collaboration aims to advance the development of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket.

title: Two Galileo Satellites Enter Service for Europe
summary: Two new Galileo satellites, SAT 33 and SAT 34, have entered service, enhancing Europe's satellite navigation system. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced their operational status, boosting the system's capability and resilience.

title: Telco CEOs Shut Down the Idea of Satellite MVNO, Say LEO Isn’t a Threat to Broadband
summary: Top telco CEOs dismissed the idea of forming an MVNO agreement with satellite operators, stating they do not view LEO satellite broadband as a significant competitive threat to traditional broadband services.

title: Space Is Coming for Silicon
summary: SpaceX has introduced Starmind, an AI satellite megaconstellation, marking a significant step in orbital data centers. Elon Musk has highlighted its potential, positioning it as a major development in the space industry.

title: Iceye and KT SAT Partner on Flood Intelligence in South Korea
summary: Iceye and KT SAT have formed a strategic partnership to provide flood monitoring solutions in South Korea for government and commercial entities. This collaboration represents the first deployment of Iceye's solutions in the country.

title: Intellian Releases New Terminal for Iridium GMDSS Service
summary: Intellian has launched a new terminal for Iridium's GMDSS maritime safety service, utilizing the Iridium Certus 100 service. The terminal was announced on Thursday.

title: Frequency Electronics Reports Increased Demand From Proliferated Satellite Programs
summary: Frequency Electronics reports $18 million in recent contract wins, including an $11 million award from an undisclosed major aerospace prime contractor to support a proliferated satellite program.

title: FCC Approves a New C-Band Auction
summary: The FCC approved a new C-band auction to clear 160 megahertz of the upper C-band spectrum, building on previous auctions. This move aims to further allocate spectrum for wireless services.

title: Lite Coms Wins $22M Contract to Support Operational Readiness
summary: Lite Coms secured a $22 million contract from an unnamed government and defense customer to provide satellite communications for operational readiness. The company specializes in integration and manufacturing of satellite communication solutions.

title: FCC Overhauls Satellite Licensing, Adopts ‘Assembly Line’ Approach
summary: The FCC approved a major overhaul of its satellite and earth station licensing process, introducing a streamlined 'licensing assembly line' approach to expedite approvals. This reform aims to modernize and accelerate the regulatory framework for space industry operations.
